messages:
Michael: Heads up — ran nsys + perfetto on the randomized batch sampler rollout, saw a weird tail spike on the 8xA100 fleet.
Anya: nice, which run? can you paste the nsys command and a short summary?
Michael: ran on canary pool 3, sampling traffic for 20 minutes. command:
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --output=rbatch_canary3 --sample=cpu,io --force true --wait=5 --duration=1200 --capture-range=nvtx
```
summary: p50 unchanged, p95 went +18% and p99 +34% for gpt-7b-ish model under steady qps.
Devin: that’s big. do we have a timeline screenshot? where are the hotspots?
Michael: attaching perfetto slice logs (excerpt) — but short: increased kernel launch rate, more stray small kernels at tail, and KV-cache misses spiking right before many of those kernels.
Sam: kv-cache misses? I thought randomized sampler was supposed to increase prefix reuse by desync-ing user sequences.
Anya: theory: randomizing cutpoints reduced cohort alignment, but it also desynced KV prefetch windows from our batch start heuristic — result: some requests miss prefetch and then cause synchronous KV loads that stall queue and trigger tiny fallback kernels.
Michael: exactly. nsys timeline shows long CPU wait (spin) while waiting for cudaMemcpy to finish — timeline snippet:
```
[600.3s] CPU thread waiting for cudaMemcpyAsync (small, per-request)
[600.302s] cudaMemcpyAsync launch
[600.305s] Kernel A (matmul_small) launches in rapid succession
[600.307s] Kernel B (softmax_small) follows
```
and then a gap where queue time climbs; overall we see many small kernels instead of the expected larger fused kernels.
Devin: are the small kernels due to quantized fallback or kernel selection heuristics seeing short seqlen? random sampler changes seqlen distribution at the boundary.
Michael: yes — kernel selector picks different code paths when sequence length distribution shifts. The sampler introduces more short-lived requests at batch edges, which our kernel selector maps to non-fused matmul paths (lower throughput) — leading to more kernel switches.
perf-bot: (automated) nsys metrics: avg kernel launch density +12%, context switches +6%, device memcpy time per-request +22%.
Sam: did you correlate with KV cache hit rate over same period?
Michael: pulled kv metrics via internal trace. Before rollout: kv_hit ~87% on warm traffic. During randomized sampler run: kv_hit dropped to 71% for the affected shards for early-window requests. The miss pattern aligns with the randomized cutpoint offsets.
Anya: interesting. so both batching and kvcache alignment matter. proposal: add a small adaptive prefetch window that is keyed to sampler offset. ie when sampler selects a cutpoint at t, prefetch for sequences with offset < Xms.
Devin: or simpler: make sampler deterministic within micro-batches of N requests so we don't desync prefetch globally. that keeps prefix reuse while avoiding global misalignment.
Michael: quick experiment idea: run A/B for 1h with: A) randomized sampler (current) B) randomized-with-local-determinism (seeded per micro-batch). measure p50/p95/p99, kv_hit, kernel_launch_density.
Sam: also test changing kernel selector threshold for short seq to prefer fused path when the batch contains mix of short+long. maybe the selector is too brittle.
Anya: actionable steps I can take this afternoon:
1) add nvtx markers around prefetch and sampler decision points so they show up in nsys/perfetto.
2) instrument per-request kvcache hit/miss tagged with sampler-offset metadata.
3) run 30m A/B on canary3 with metrics dashboard capturing p50/p95/p99 and kv_hit.

Michael: I'll roll a canary with the nvtx markers and collect a high-res nsys run (30s captures at peak). snippet to add markers:
```
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("sampler_decide offset=%d", offset_ms);
... sampler logic ...
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("kvcache_prefetch start");
... prefetch async launch ...
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```

Devin: for nsys config, add `--sample=all` and enable `--cpuctxsw` if possible to capture the CPU scheduling impact.
Sam: one-off observation: perfetto shows a tight band of CPU spinning in the scheduler thread (~10ms) which correlates with those memcpy waits — probably our thread affinity causes co-location with network NAPI bursts.
Michael: noted. affinity adjustment + prefetch alignment might reduce device memcpy tail. I'll also try aligning prefetch launches to a dedicated prefetch worker thread pinned away from network IRQs.
Anya: questions for next sync: expected perf delta threshold for rollout? we should keep p95 within +5% vs baseline. if A/B fails, revert and implement the deterministic micro-batch seeding.
Devin: SGTM. add ticket with experiments and rollback plan.
Michael: created ticket INF-3247 with steps and links to captures. I'll paste the nsys output summary later.
perf-bot: (automated) capture links: gs://perf/runs/rbatch_canary3_1718533333.nsys -> uploaded
Sam: thanks — looks like we have a solid hypothesis: randomized sampler desynced kv-prefetch -> kv miss -> small kernel launches -> kernel thrash -> tail latency.
Anya: good work. next: run A/B and iterate on prefetch alignment. :thumbsup: 
Michael: I'll post results in this thread once we have the 1h A/B.
Devin: thanks team.
